lastText: File ClosedThe Salient, Sealed TwiceContestedAllied Combined Chiefs, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more ███████ Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more ██████████ road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. Tehran ended hedged rather than committed: Overlord promised in principle with the █████████████ fine print intact, and Stalin's standing suspicion of the West fed at exactly the moment the historical conference starved it. The stand in the Peloponnese broke and the beaches were lost, and what the Germans took in Greece was a ████████ or more instead of the real 14,000. The █████████████ Fleet was sent against the German convoys off Crete, as it was, and paid three cruisers and six destroyers for an island that was lost ██████. What was really being decided, choice by choice, was never whether ███████ lost, only what the peace on the other side of it would look like.One Year LaterA year past ███████ in ██████, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences (Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended) settled or failed to settle in advance.
